## About

Andrew Mathews is a student, builder and systems thinker based in Dubai. He works across artificial intelligence, software development, robotics, product design and engineering competitions. He started building with robotics at age 9 through the Mbot@IHS programme, and from there moved deeper into software, AI, computer vision and product development. Today he builds everything from small Python experiments to full product systems such as Gradr, TerraCart and ClientFlow OS, competes in STEM and engineering challenges, takes part in MUN conferences, works on F1 in Schools / STEM Racing, and shows projects at exhibitions.

Working principles:

- Systems Over Features: I like building connected systems that solve a complete problem instead of isolated features.
- Ship First, Improve Always: A working product gives me something real to learn from. I build, test, iterate, and improve.
- Real Problems First: The best projects start with a problem worth solving.

### Long · first person

I'm Andrew Mathews, a student developer and AI builder from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and a student at The Indian High School, Dubai. I don't just learn technology — I apply it. I started building in 2022 at age 9 through the Mbot@IHS robotics programme, where I built and presented an original model at a school exhibition. That gave me the instinct to build physically; from there I moved deeper into software, AI, computer vision and product development.

Today I work across AI applications and assistants, full-stack web products, robotics and engineering, and data work. My flagship products are Gradr, an AI career accelerator; Stack Up, a personal-finance app built around gamification; TerraCart, a sustainable shopping assistant; and ClientFlow OS, a business operating system. Alongside them sits a larger archive of tools and experiments.

Outside of building, I compete in STEM and engineering challenges — Techfest, FIRST LEGO League and F1 in Schools / STEM Racing — take part in Model United Nations conferences, and demonstrate projects at exhibitions. I care about systems over features, shipping over theory, and starting from a problem worth solving.

### Long · third person

Andrew Mathews is a student developer and AI builder from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and a student at The Indian High School, Dubai. He describes his approach simply: he does not just learn technology, he applies it. He started building in 2022 at age 9 through the Mbot@IHS robotics programme, where he built and presented an original model at a school exhibition — the beginning of a move from hardware into software, AI, computer vision and product development.

He works across AI applications and assistants, full-stack web products, robotics and engineering, and data work. His flagship products are Gradr, an AI career accelerator; Stack Up, a personal-finance app built around gamification; TerraCart, a sustainable shopping assistant; and ClientFlow OS, a business operating system, alongside a larger archive of tools and experiments.

Outside of building, he competes in STEM and engineering challenges — Techfest, FIRST LEGO League and F1 in Schools / STEM Racing — takes part in Model United Nations conferences, and demonstrates projects at exhibitions. His working principles are systems over features, shipping first and improving always, and starting from a real problem.

### Gradr

- Category: Career Technology · AI
- Status: Building
- Tech: AI, React
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/gradr
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/gradr.json

An AI-powered career accelerator designed to help students, graduates, and early-career professionals build stronger resumes, prepare for interviews, and manage their career journey.

Problem: Early-career candidates get almost no useful feedback. Resumes disappear into applicant tracking systems without explanation, interview practice is either expensive or unstructured, and applications end up scattered across spreadsheets, inboxes and browser tabs. The missing piece is not more advice — it is a system that reviews your material, tells you exactly what is weak, and keeps the whole search in one place.



Results:
- Status: In active development — Core flows working end to end.
- Core modules: 6 — Resume, ATS, interviews, tracker, analytics, plan.
- Feedback loop: Analyse → practise → apply — One connected system.
- Integrations: MCP tools — Resumes, jobs and reminders exposed to assistants.

---

### Stack Up

- Category: Personal Finance · Gamification
- Status: Live
- Tech: React
- Live: https://stackup-app.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/stack-up
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/stack-up.json

The first product I shipped. A personal finance system designed to make spending, budgeting, and saving easier to understand and more engaging.

Problem: Most budgeting apps assume you already have the discipline they are supposed to build. They show you a pie chart after the money is gone. Stack Up started from the opposite question: what would make a student actually open a finance app on a normal Tuesday? The answer was progress — visible streaks, goals that move, and numbers small enough to act on.



Results:
- Status: Live — Publicly usable at stackup-app.base44.app.
- First shipped product: 2024 — Idea to deployed app end to end.
- Core modules: 5 — Expenses, budgets, goals, streaks, analytics.
- Entry time: < 10s — Design target for logging a spend.

---

### TerraCart

- Category: AI · Sustainability · E-commerce
- Status: Developing
- Tech: AI, Browser Extension
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/terracart
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/terracart.json

An AI-powered shopping assistant designed to help people discover more sustainable alternatives while shopping online.

Problem: Shopping sustainably online is mostly guesswork. Product pages optimise for conversion, claims are unverifiable, and comparing a greener alternative means opening five tabs mid-checkout. TerraCart puts the analysis where the decision happens — on the product page — and offers a concrete alternative instead of a lecture.



Results:
- Status: In development — Analysis and alternatives in progress.
- Surface: Browser extension — Works inline on product pages.
- Principle: Evidence over scores — Unverified claims labelled as such.

---

### ClientFlow OS

- Category: Business Operating System · AI
- Status: In Active Development
- Tech: AI, React
- Source: https://github.com/andrewmkbuilds/ClientFlow-OS
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/clientflow-os
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/clientflow-os.json

A unified platform for managing clients, projects, conversations, payments, documents, and workflows in one connected system.

Problem: Small studios and freelancers run their business across six tools that do not talk: a CRM, a chat app, a spreadsheet of projects, an invoicing tool, a drive folder and a notes app. Every handoff between them is manual and every status question costs a search. ClientFlow OS collapses the client lifecycle — enquiry to delivery to payment — into one connected system.



Results:
- Status: In active development — Core lifecycle working.
- Modules: 8 — Clients, projects, comms, payments, docs, automation.
- Payments: Stripe — Webhook-driven state.
- Code: Public repo — github.com/andrewmkbuilds/ClientFlow-OS

---

### Scholara

- Category: Education · School OS · AI
- Status: Live
- Tech: AI, Base44
- Live: https://get-scholara.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/scholara
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/scholara.json

An AI-powered school operating system that unites academics, operations, communication and analytics for students, teachers, parents and school leaders.

Problem: A school runs academics, finance, transport, wellbeing and parent communication across spreadsheets, disconnected apps and paper forms. Scholara replaces that patchwork with one system where every role — student, teacher, parent, administrator, principal, counselor, finance staff, librarian and transport manager — works over the same data with its own dashboard, navigation and permissions.



Results:
- Roles: 9+ — Product scope as published on the site.
- Modules: 30+ — Product scope as published on the site.
- AI features: 15+ — Product scope as published on the site.
- Try it: Open demo — Pick any role and use the full platform.

### CritiqueFlow

- Category: Design Tooling · Review
- Status: Live
- Tech: React, Base44
- Live: https://critiqueflow.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/critiqueflow
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/critiqueflow.json

A design review platform that turns visual feedback into structured discussion, tasks and a measurable design health score.

Problem: Design feedback usually arrives as loose comments in chat, scattered screenshots and calls nobody writes down. It is hard to act on, impossible to measure, and the same comment comes back in the next round. CritiqueFlow puts the design on a canvas and turns every note into something with an owner, a state and a score attached to it.



Results:
- Scan: Deterministic — Checks are computed from the feedback data.
- Core loop: Feedback → task → fix — Each note becomes a tracked item.
- Compare: Two versions — Before/after slider on the same canvas.

---

### The Neon Rush

- Category: Game · Interactive
- Status: Live
- Tech: Game, Base44
- Live: https://the-neonrush.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/the-neonrush
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/the-neonrush.json

A neon arcade game built around story chapters, daily missions, mini-games and a hangar of ships and skins.

Problem: A game needs a reason to come back on a normal Tuesday, not just a good first level. The Neon Rush wraps its arcade play in a command center — chapters, objectives, records and unlocks — so a short session always has a next thing to chase.



Results:
- Modes: Story · Arcade · Daily — Three ways into the same game.
- Progression: Ships & skins — Unlocks earned through play.
- Status: Live — Playable in the browser.

### Horizon Motorsports

- Category: Racing / Community
- Status: Active
- Tech: React, Framer Motion
- Live: https://horizonmotorsports.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/horizon-motorsports
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/horizon-motorsports.json

Digital home for Horizon Motorsports, a UAE-based racing team competing in FLL, Techfest, and engineering competitions.

Problem: Horizon Motorsports needed a presence that matched how the team actually operates: a Dubai-based racing and engineering team competing in FLL, Techfest and other UAE competitions, with a following that lives mostly on social. The site had to work as the anchor visitors land on from Instagram — fast, motion-driven, and clear about who the team is and what it competes in.



Results:
- Status: Active — Live team site.
- Competitions: FLL · Techfest — UAE engineering and robotics circuit.
- Base: Dubai, UAE — Team operates locally.
- Primary channel: Instagram — Site is the landing point for social traffic.

### DevOS

- Category: Productivity / AI
- Status: Live
- Tech: Python, AI Integration
- Live: https://dev-os-flow.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/devos
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/devos.json

AI-powered developer command center designed to bring tasks, focus sessions, and project threads into one place.

Problem: Building alone means context lives in five places at once — a task list, a terminal, a notes file, a chat with an AI assistant, and whatever was open when you stopped. DevOS came out of my own workflow: one command center where the task, the focus session and the project thread are the same object, so picking work back up does not require reconstructing it.



Results:
- Status: Live — Usable at dev-os-flow.base44.app.
- Objects unified: 3 — Tasks, focus sessions, project threads.
- Built for: Solo builders — Designed around my own workflow.
- Interaction: Keyboard-first — Command-driven navigation.

---

### COGNOS

- Category: Cognitive / AI
- Status: Live
- Tech: AI APIs, NLP, Graph Architecture
- Live: https://cognos-app.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/cognos
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/cognos.json

An AI cognitive operating system designed to capture raw thoughts, classify them, and map connections between ideas.

Problem: Notes apps store text; they do not store thinking. Ideas arrive unformed, at bad times, and the connection between two of them is usually the valuable part. COGNOS was an attempt to build a capture surface that classifies a raw thought the moment it lands and then shows how it relates to everything captured before.



Results:
- Status: Live — Usable at cognos-app.base44.app.
- Pipeline: Capture → classify → connect — Fully automatic.
- Link quality: Embedding-based — Replaced keyword matching.

---

### TabZen

- Category: Productivity / Browser
- Status: Live
- Tech: Browser Extension, AI Summarization
- Live: https://tabzen.base44.app/
- Case study: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects/tabzen
- JSON: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/data/v1/projects/tabzen.json

Intelligent tab management that groups tabs by context, summarizes them, and archives them without losing information.

Problem: Research sessions end with forty tabs and no memory of why half of them were opened. Closing them loses the thread; keeping them makes the browser unusable. TabZen treats tabs as a working set that should be grouped, summarised and archived without losing the reason each one existed.



Results:
- Status: Live — Usable at tabzen.base44.app.
- Core loop: Group → summarise → archive — Three-step workflow.
- Data loss: Zero by design — Archive precedes close.

---

## FAQ

### Who is Andrew Mathews?

Andrew Mathews is a student developer and technology builder based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. He studies at The Indian High School, Dubai, and has been building since age 9, starting with robotics and moving into software, AI and product development.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/about

### What does Andrew build?

AI applications and assistants, full web applications and tools, robotics and engineering projects, computer-vision experiments, and product systems taken from a rough concept through to something that runs.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/skills

### What technologies does he work with?

Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, React and Flutter, generative-AI models and APIs, OpenCV and MediaPipe for computer vision, and hardware and sensor work from competition robotics. The skills page lists the full set.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/skills

### Which projects are on this site?

Nineteen projects are documented as case studies. The four featured ones are Gradr, an AI career accelerator; Stack Up, a personal-finance app with gamification; TerraCart, a sustainable shopping assistant; and ClientFlow OS, a business operating system. The rest form the project archive.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/projects

### What is AndrewBuilds?

AndrewBuilds is the name Andrew uses for his work and his online profiles — it is the wordmark on this site and the handle behind his GitHub, Linktree and build-platform accounts. It is a personal practice, not a company or an agency.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/profile

### What has he won?

Competition results published here are: 1st Place Data Science and 2nd Place IoT at Techfest, 2nd Place Space Tech at Group Techfest, an Innovation Award at the FLL UAE Dubai Regional, 2nd Place at the "Math & Me" Math Expo, and 3rd Place Shot Put at the Annual Athletic Meet. In Model United Nations his only award is a Verbal Commendation, at IHSMUN 2025, Novara MUN 2026 and the IHS UNSummit 2026. No other MUN award is claimed.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/achievements

### How did he start building?

With the Mbot@IHS robotics programme in 2022, at age 9, building and presenting an original model at a school exhibition. The journey page records the milestones from there.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/journey

### How can someone get in touch?

Through the contact page, which has a working form, or through any of the public profiles linked in the site footer and on the profile page.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/contact

### How was this website built?

It is a TanStack Start application with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Motion, rendering server-side. The colophon documents the stack, the design system and the ambient background in detail.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/colophon

### Can this site's information be read by developers or AI agents?

Yes. A read-only, versioned JSON API is published under /data/v1, alongside /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /agents.md and an OpenAPI description. Everything it exposes is public information already on the site.

Source: https://andrewmk.is-a.dev/developers
